title: Indexes
objective: See why an index speeds up finding rows, and what it costs on every write.

sources.title: PostgreSQL documentation: Indexes, Introduction (indexes speed up reads and add overhead to writes)

simplifies: The index is shown as a sorted list searched with binary search. Real databases use B-trees (and other kinds), keep them on disk in pages, and the query planner decides whether using the index is actually cheaper than a scan.

quiz.prompt: A table has 1,000,000 rows and an index on email. Finding one email takes roughly…

options.explanation: Right. A sorted index halves the search each step: about log₂ 1,000,000.
That is a full scan, which the index avoids.
It still has to narrow down the position.

options.text: Every insert and update must also update every index, so writes get slower
options.explanation: Right. Indexes speed up reads but add work (and space) to every write.
They make the reads they are used for faster.
They allow many; the cost is the reason to choose.
